quest.title: The Darkbrood
quest.description: You left the Amethyst Athenaeum fairly quickly. One possible reason for your haste that I could fathom was perhaps to spare yourself from murdering the Acolyte. His belated revelation that the stolen books could be tracked magically left you feeling a tad irksome I would imagine! Nevertheless, you quickly made your way to the area he had indicated hoping to finally track down the mysterious villain behind the Fetish.

node.tag: Find the Books in the Church
node.journal_entry: An oddly unadorned church drew you inside. The lack of idols or images seemed deliberate, almost as if the emptiness itself was a thing of worship. Inside the building you located a chest with $[Vendors.q09_quest_acolyte_librarian_Name]'s missing tomes. It seemed that you had finally discovered your elusive villains!

node.instruction: Go to the area marked on your map.
node.journal_entry: The location you arrived at was odd, even by my standards. Various dark, dwarf-like beings were walking about, patrolling and working in an eerie silence. Finding the books was your current priority but, given that the entire Dwarven race was believed to have been wiped out, it couldn't hurt to dig a little deeper too.

action.tag: An Add Quest Area to World-Map Action

node.journal_entry: The eerie, hand shaped altar pulsed with a dark presence. Even as you approached you could hear an insidious whispering, just on the edge of your mind, beckoning you ever closer. Reaching out, you had barely touched the structure when the voice erupted in your mind. You had the impression that it was not addressing you, perhaps not even aware of your presence because it was so saturated. It was an amalgam of voices, of minds, all whispering over each other and clamoring into your consciousness like a thousand bees pouring into your skull. You broke contact...

action.tag: A Start Client SFX on Player Action

node.journal_entry: The forge seemed to draw your eye from the start, something was simply out of place about it. The tools and half finished weapons around it definitely resembled those you found in the Sadayel camp earlier but there was also something more. A feeling of power emanated from here, something that felt old, forgotten, but biding its time...

Their magics struck just as hard and precisely as their weapons. The darkbrood, you would later learn, functioned through a hive mind. A dark pact with a greedy god that went horribly wrong (at least for the god, poor twisted and ever-ravenous Sahul...)

task.tag: A Take Damage from Skill Task

node.journal_entry: Why were they here however, and who were the denizens of this odd place. I never claimed to understand your methods, but I assume you had to test them a little, see what they were made of. Either that, or you felt like a fight!

These were no ordinary Dwarves. The cold, dead eyes that peered right into your soul were a stark contrast to the almost bestial rage that fueled their unnaturally cohesive attack strategies. They moved as one, struck as one... you did not know it at the time, but you had just encountered the Darkbrood.

task.tag: A Take Damage from Object Task

node.journal_entry: You had Behrem's missing tomes and you finally had someone dark and sinister enough to qualify as the villain of your tale. What you did not have, however, was motive...and that meant you also had more questions.
It was time to return to the Shamman. Questions and books alike belonged there.
